A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PvP/SRL4Humanoid study and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. v2 retains Appendices A–C and adds Appendix D, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original humanoid-control experiments, including learning curves, tracking performance, SRL ablations, and robot demonstrations in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds teacher–student comparisons, additional robot and terrain evaluations, and coefficient-sensitivity results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The zero-masking procedure, shared encoder, SimSiam-style objective, PPO integration, and interval updates remain unchanged. The new coefficient study does not change the baseline coefficient of 0.5 specified in Appendix C.2.

E1.justification: Appendix D.2 adds LimX Oli velocity tracking on rough terrain and velocity tracking on the Unitree G1 robot. These substantially broaden coverage beyond the original flat-terrain tracking and motion-imitation tasks on one robot platform.

E2.justification: Figures 13–15 introduce TSD-Teacher, TSD-Student, and proprioception-only PPO comparisons, including on the original LimX tasks. This adds a distinct privileged-learning alternative and an information-availability control. The original PPO/VAE/SPR/SimSiam comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce a proprioception-only control, two-stage teacher–student comparisons, and wall-clock efficiency evaluation for G1 in Figure 16. Original task settings and PPO hyperparameters remain unchanged; relabeling existing training axes as iterations does not establish a changed budget.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds analyses of privileged-information dependence, distillation versus joint learning, rough-terrain performance, and sensitivity to the PvP loss coefficient. v1 already disclosed searching coefficients 0.1, 0.5, and 1.0, but did not report their comparative learning curves.

E5.justification: Both versions describe learning curves using means and standard-deviation bands. The additional figures follow that existing practice; neither version specifies run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 13–17 add substantial results: PvP exceeds distilled students, proprioception-only PPO learns poorly, G1 converges faster with PvP, and coefficient 0.1 gives the highest final score in the coefficient sweep. Teachers sometimes achieve higher final scores than PvP. These are additional results, not demonstrated v1-to-v2 performance gains.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, objectives in Equations 1–12, and reward formulas remain unchanged. Appendix D adds empirical findings and conceptual arguments, without new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: proprioceptive–privileged contrastive learning, the SRL4Humanoid framework, and improved humanoid learning efficiency and performance. Additional experiments support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds explanations involving teacher-imposed limitations, restricted exploration, and joint evolution of representations and policies, plus interpretations of privileged-information and coefficient effects. The original limitations concerning additional SRL methods and visual inputs remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-repository link and identifies the experimental GPU as an RTX4090 with 24GB memory, whereas v1 specified only a single GPU. These are additional access and hardware disclosures, not evidence of changed original experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Kumar et al.'s RMA and Lee et al.'s challenging-terrain locomotion work, positioning PvP against teacher–student distillation in Appendix D. The existing related-work discussion is otherwise substantively retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and terminology corrections, updates author affiliations and contact information, adds acknowledgments, and introduces Appendix D. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds a substantial set of comparison and sensitivity plots in Figures 13–17. Existing learning plots switch from percentage progress to iteration axes, erroneous 32dof titles become 31dof, and figures and appendix material are reflowed. Tables 1–6 retain their structure.

improvement.justification: Appendix D substantially strengthens validation previously limited to SRL comparisons on one robot by adding distillation comparisons, privileged-information controls, rough terrain, and a second platform. Coefficient analysis and code/hardware disclosures further improve assessability. New experimental details remain sparse, and some superiority language exceeds the final-score advantages in Figures 15–16, but these limitations do not outweigh the broader empirical support.
